etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English recommenden, from Old French recommender (compare French recommander), from Latin re- + commendāre (“to commend, commit; to recommend”), from con- +‎ mandāre (“commit, intrust, enjoin”), from manus (“hand, handwriting, power”) +‎ dare (“to give; to offer or render”).

definitions.definition: (transitive) To bestow commendation on; to represent favourably; to suggest, endorse or encourage as an appropriate choice.
(transitive) To make acceptable; to attract favor to.
(transitive, archaic) To commit, confide to another's care, confidence or acceptance, with favoring representations

quote.citation: 1896 November – 1897 May, Rudyard Kipling, “Captains Courageous”, Garden City, N.Y.: Doubleday & Company, published 1897, →OCLC:
quote.text: "I'm glad to have a recommend from that quarter. Airheart's skipper of the San Jose now.  […] "
